notes.summary: In coding-decoding, a word, number or sentence is written in a secret code. You find the rule from the example and use it on a new word. SSC asks 2 to 3 coding questions in almost every Tier 1 shift. Nearly every code is one of six kinds: letter shift, opposite letters, rearranged letters, letters to numbers, sentence codes or substitution.

concepts.title: The method for every coding question
concepts.body:
1. Write the word and its code one above the other, letter under letter.
  2. Write the alphabet position above each letter.
  3. Compare place by place. Is each letter moved by a number? Is it the opposite letter? Are the same letters just in a new order?
  4. Check the rule on every letter, and on the second example if one is given.
  5. Apply the rule to the new word. Then look at the options: often only one has the right first and last letters.

concepts.title: Alphabet positions
concepts.body:
LetterABCDEFGHIJKLM
From A12345678910111213
From Z26252423222120191817161514
LetterNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
From A14151617181920212223242526
From Z13121110987654321
EJOTY: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25. Count from the nearest one (P = O + 1 = 16).
Reverse position (from Z) = 27 − position. Opposite pairs: A–Z, B–Y, C–X, D–W, E–V, F–U, G–T, H–S, I–R, J–Q, K–P, L–O, M–N.
Wrap-around: after Z comes A. Y + 3 = B; B − 3 = Y.

concepts.title: Letter shift patterns
concepts.body:
PatternWord → code
Same shiftCAT → DBU (+1 each)
Same shift backwardDOG → BME (−2 each)
Growing shiftPENCIL → QGQGNR (+1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6)
Alternate shiftFACED → GZDDE (+1, −1, +1, −1, +1)
Shift equal to word lengthPAPER → UFUJW (+5, five letters)
Do the work letter by letter. Writing positions takes ten seconds and avoids most errors.

concepts.title: Opposite-letter codes
concepts.body:
Each letter is swapped with its opposite (the two add up to 27).
GOLD → TLOW because G (7) ↔ T (20), O (15) ↔ L (12), L ↔ O, D (4) ↔ W (23).
Spot it fast: if A becomes Z, or M becomes N, think "opposite" first. Sometimes the opposite letters are also written in reverse order, so check the order too.

concepts.title: Rearranged letters
concepts.body:
If the code has the same letters as the word, only the order has changed.
PatternWord → code
Whole word reversedGARDEN → NEDRAG
Pairs swappedCREATION → RC AE IT NO
Each half reversedMOTHER → TOM REH
First and last swappedSTAMP → PTAMS
Some codes do two things: rearrange and then shift each letter by 1. Write the positions to see both steps.

concepts.title: Letters to numbers
concepts.body:
MethodExample
Positions side by sideBAD → 2 1 4 → 214; LAMINATE → 12 1 13 9 14 1 20 5
Sum of positionsCAT = 3 + 1 + 20 = 24
Sum × a numberTOP = (20 + 15 + 16) × 2 = 102; BAD = 7 × 2 = 14
Sum of reverse positionsSET = 8 + 22 + 7 = 37; MIX = 14 + 18 + 3 = 35
Reverse sum + number of lettersPAINT = 75 + 5 = 80; DROP = 55 + 4 = 59
Product of positionsCAB = 3 × 1 × 2 = 6
Start with the plain sum. If the code is bigger, try sum × number of letters or a product. If the numbers look odd, try reverse positions.

concepts.title: Sentence codes
concepts.body:
Each word in a sentence gets a code word, but the codes may be in a different order.
  1. Take two sentences that share one word.
  2. The code they share is that word's code.
  3. Repeat until you reach the asked word.
Example: 'tea is hot' = 'ka la ma', 'hot and cold' = 'ra ma sa', 'cold tea please' = 'ka sa pi'. Tea is in sentences 1 and 3; the shared code is ka, so tea = ka. Hot = ma (1 and 2). Cold = sa (2 and 3).

Number of letters: sometimes the code is just the letter count of each word. 'complete the drawing' = 837 (8, 3, 7 letters). So 'kindly stand straight' = 658.

concepts.title: Substitution
concepts.body:
Here a word is "called" another word. Read the real-world answer first, then replace it with its code name.
If water is called pot, then fish live in "pot". The trap is to answer with the word that pot is called, or with the real word. Answer with the name the real thing has in that language.

concepts.title: Decoding and codes of codes
concepts.body:
• Decoding: if the code of a word is given and you must find the word, apply the rule backwards (+2 becomes −2).
  • "How is the code coded?" If BRAVE is CSBWF (+1), then CSBWF itself is coded by applying +1 again: DTCXG.
  • Option check: for long words, code only the first two and last two letters and match them with the options.

varieties.name: Letter shift
varieties.how: Write the positions of the word and the code. Find the shift for each letter: it can be the same, growing (+1, +2, +3) or alternating (+1, −1). Apply the same shifts to the new word.

example.q: FACED is written as GZDDE. How is LABOR written?
steps: F → G is +1, A → Z is −1, C → D is +1, E → D is −1, D → E is +1. The shift alternates +1, −1.

varieties.name: Opposite letters
varieties.how: Check whether each pair of letters adds up to 27 (A–Z, M–N). If yes, replace each letter of the new word with its opposite.

example.q: GOLD is written as TLOW. How is SILVER written?
steps: G (7) + T (20) = 27, O (15) + L (12) = 27: opposite letters.
S → H, I → R, L → O, V → E, E → V, R → I.

varieties.name: Rearranged letters
varieties.how: If the code has the same letters, number the letter places (1, 2, 3 …) and write which place moved where. Apply the same moves to the new word.

example.q: CREATION is written as RCAEITNO. How is SEQUENCE written?
steps: Split into pairs: CR EA TI ON. Each pair is swapped: RC AE IT NO.
SEQUENCE in pairs: SE QU EN CE.
Swap each pair: ES UQ NE EC.

varieties.name: Letters to numbers
varieties.how: Try the sum of positions, then sum × a number, reverse positions, positions written side by side, or product. Confirm with both examples.

example.q: TOP is coded as 102 and BAD as 14. How is DOG coded?

varieties.name: Sentence codes
varieties.how: Compare two sentences that share exactly one word; their shared code belongs to that word. If codes are numbers, check whether each digit is the letter count of a word.

example.q: 'tea is hot' = 'ka la ma', 'hot and cold' = 'ra ma sa', 'cold tea please' = 'ka sa pi'. What is the code for 'tea'?
steps: Tea appears in sentence 1 and sentence 3.
The only code in both is 'ka'.

varieties.name: Substitution
varieties.how: Answer the real question first (fish live in water). Then find what that real word is called in the code language.

example.q: Sky is called cloud, cloud is called thunder, thunder is called water, water is called pot, pot is called desert, desert is called sky. Where do fish live?

tips: Always write letter positions above both the word and the code; most errors come from counting in your head.
Check the first and last letters of the options first. Often only one option survives.
If A becomes Z or M becomes N, think opposite letters.
If the code has the same letters as the word, it is a rearrangement; number the places.
For number codes, try the plain sum first, then reverse positions, then products.
In sentence codes, start with the word that appears in exactly two sentences.
In substitution, answer the real question first, then translate.
traps: Forgetting wrap-around: after Z comes A (X + 4 = B).
Using a rule that fits the first letters only. Check every letter.
In substitution, giving the real word ("water") instead of its code name ("pot").
In decoding, applying the rule forwards instead of backwards.
In sentence codes, the order of code words is not the order of the words.

questions.q: In a certain code language, CAT is written as DBU. How will DOG be written in that language?
questions.solution:
C→D, A→B, T→U: each letter +1.
D+1 = E, O+1 = P, G+1 = H.
DOG → EPH.

questions.q: In a certain code, BAD is written as 214. How will FED be written in that code?
questions.solution:
Each letter is replaced by its position: B=2, A=1, D=4.
F=6, E=5, D=4.
FED → 654.

questions.q: In a certain code language, PAPER is written as SDSHU. How will PENCIL be written in that language?
questions.solution:
P→S, A→D, P→S, E→H, R→U: each letter +3.
P+3 = S, E+3 = H, N+3 = Q, C+3 = F, I+3 = L, L+3 = O.
PENCIL → SHQFLO.

questions.q: In a certain code language, GARDEN is written as NEDRAG. How will FLOWER be written in that language?
questions.solution:
GARDEN written backwards is NEDRAG: the word is reversed.
FLOWER reversed = REWOLF.

questions.q: If 'sky' is called 'sea', 'sea' is called 'water', 'water' is called 'air' and 'air' is called 'cloud', then where do fish live?
questions.solution:
Fish live in water.
In this language, water is called 'air'.
So the answer is Air.

questions.q: In a certain code language, LAMP is written as OZNK. How will DESK be written in that language?
questions.solution:
L(12)→O(15), A(1)→Z(26), M(13)→N(14), P(16)→K(11): positions add to 27, so each letter becomes its opposite letter.
D(4)→W(23), E(5)→V(22), S(19)→H(8), K(11)→P(16).
DESK → WVHP.

flashcards.back: Positions add to 27: A–Z, M–N, D–W, K–P
Find the real answer, then reply with its code name.
After Z comes A: X + 4 = B
